newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO WIDEN GAP TO SEVEN POINTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO WIDEN GAP TO SEVEN POINTS.

text.p: Brazilian Anderson inspired Monaco to a 2-0 victory over Paris Saint-Germain that lifted them seven points clear in the French first division on Sunday.
Anderson scored a superb second goal in the 71st minute to snuff out any ideas second-placed PSG had of hauling themselves back into the game.
Nigerian substitute Victor Ikpeba, who had come on only 11 minutes earlier for Scotland's John Collins, found Anderson with a fine long ball out of defence on the right.
The Brazilian, having beaten the offside trap, shook off Bruno N'Gotty's late challenge to shoot past goalkeeper Bernard Lama and in off the far post.

The striker had the clearest chance of the first half when he brought a diving save from Lama with a low shot one minute before the interval after being put through by midfielder Ali Benarbia on the right.
Anderson also had the first shot on target of the match, a 23rd minute effort which Lama was well placed to hold.

Monaco opened with a goal from a close range downward header by midfielder Sylvain Legwinski from a corner by the influential Benarbia in the 64th minute. Lama managed to get an arm to the ball but it went in off the near post.
"What was at stake affected the game for the first hour, but the first goal, which was a bit lucky, opened things up," Monaco general manager Henri Biancheri said.
"In the end it was a logical result, but the road is still long (to the end of the season)."

Striker Ikpeba, whose inclusion for the last half-hour after Collins' busy defensive work signalled Monaco coach Jean Tigana's belief they could win the match, could have made it three but his 87th minute shot came back off the bar.
Collins said: "The coach's decision was courageous to change tactics at that moment. It could have failed but it paid off. Ikpeba's entry boosted the attack."

PSG, whose midfielder Leonardo is a former Brazil youth team mate of Anderson, did not manage a single clear-cut chance even if they forced Monaco keeper Fabien Barthez to come out sharply at least twice to smother the ball at the feet of their attackers.
Four points adrift before kickoff and looking for a rehabilitating performance after a string of poor results, PSG took the game to Monaco from the start and had the better of the opening exchanges.

They did not have a bad match, but Monaco defended well, were dangerous on the left where skilful teenage striker Thierry Henry troubled PSG's right flank and lasted the pace better on a damp, energy-sapping pitch at the Louis II stadium.
PSG defender Paul Le Guen said: "We held out well for an hour, apart from one chance that fell to Anderson.
"Perhaps we weren't brilliant, but we were solid. The goal changed it all, however. It's difficult to come back, especially on such a pitch.
"We said before the match this would be the turning point in the championship."
Tigana said: "Paris Saint-Germain remain our most dangerous rivals. They have won lots of titles while we still have everything to prove."

Defending champions Auxerre won 3-2 at relegation-threatened Caen in Sunday's other match, conceding two goals in the final two minutes after looking comfortable winners. They are seventh 13 points adrift of Monaco.

Monaco - 1-Fabien Barthez; 2-Patrick Blondeau, 5-Franck Dumas, 4-Martin Djetou, 6-Emmanuel Petit; 15-Sylvain Legwinski, 18-Gilles Grimandi, 8-Ali Benarbia, 7-John Collins (24-Victor Ikpeba 60); 9-Anderson, 12-Thierry Henry (10-Enzo Scifo 85).

Paris St Germain - 1-Bernard Lama; 13-Laurent Fournier (17-Jimmy Algerino 70), 6-Paul Le Guen, 4-Bruno N'Gotty, 2-Daniel Kenedy; 8-Vincent Guerin (20-Cyrille Pouget 66), 19-Jerome Leroy, 15-Benoit Cauet, 10-Rai; 7-Leonardo, 11-Patrice Loko (9-Julio Cesar Dely Valdes 76).
